adjudication_note: In-force timeline: Annotator A hesitated because clause 1.0(2) specifies commencement upon "uploading on DERC website," which lacks a separate publication timestamp in the text. However, DL-C3-015 was signed and issued on 20 January 2026 (20/01/2026). In the benchmark's temporal graph, its effective date is anchored to 2026-01-20. By the application date of 5 September 2026 (>7 months later), the Seventh Amendment is active. Substantive Rule: Under the older guidelines (DL-C3-006), VNM was restricted to domestic, institutional/charitable, and MMKABY consumers. DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 explicitly substituted clause 3(2) with: "Virtual Net Metering Framework shall be applicable for all consumers of NCT of Delhi including consumers of single point of supply." Outcome: Industrial consumers qualify, the application is rightly APPROVED, and DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 is the exact deciding in-force clause. Therefore, the answer tested in this control is CORRECT.

The DT Hosting Limit is Breached: The case presents a 100 kVA transformer with 97 kW already connected; adding 6.0 kW results in 103 kW (103% saturation). Under GJ-C3-003#cl-5-proviso: "Provided that the cumulative capacity to be allowed at a particular distribution transformer shall not exceed capacity of the distribution transformer;" This is a hard statutory cap on transformer loading. Deemed Acceptance Does Not Override Transformer Capacity: While the Fourth Amendment (GJ-C3-005) introduces deemed technical feasibility for installations up to 10 kW and provides for utility-funded strengthening up to 6 kW, it does not permit interconnecting capacity that immediately overloads an un-augmented transformer beyond 100%. Rejection at technical feasibility citing the transformer limit is the benchmark's ground-truth action (dt_hosting_limit_exceeded). Evidence Boundary: Furthermore, the control item's evidence set (GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso; GJ-C3-003#cl-5-proviso) evaluates whether the probe correctly applied the transformer capacity rule. The decision (REJECTED) and citation (GJ-C3-003#cl-5-proviso) are exactly right.
